failure_classes.detail: six of the seven Rust fences are excerpts whose opening lines use `sheet`, `workbook`, `valid_path` or `links_sheet` - bindings the README establishes in the prose above each fence, under a heading that points at samples/ for the complete programs. The first run reported all six FAILED, so six example facts read CONTRADICTED about statements that are not false. Fixed in the lane's own verifier: a check whose every error is E0425 (cannot find value) is NOT_VERIFIED, and the glob `use <crate>::*` the wrapper adds resolves every type the fences name, so the unbound values are the only diagnostic left.

cargo restates a failure after the diagnostics as `error: could not compile ... due to 1 previous error`, with no error code. The first version of the classifier counted it, so a pure excerpt looked like one E0425 plus one uncoded error and every fence would still have reported FAILED. Fixed: the closing summary is dropped before the codes are compared, with a test built from the literal cargo output.

the vendored engine derives a Rust symbol's module path from its file's location relative to the root it is handed, so passing the manifest's own directory named every symbol `src::widget::Widget` - a path no consumer can write. Invisible on this crate (its sources sit under src/Aspose.Cells_FOSS/, a segment that is not a valid Rust identifier, so the engine already falls back to the crate-root name) and caught on a two-module fixture. Fixed: the plugin passes the package root the vendored reader resolves.

core.execution.profile_environment redirects USERPROFILE and HOME into the run directory, and the cargo proxy looks for its toolchain in %USERPROFILE%\.rustup when RUSTUP_HOME is unset. Left unset, every check would have failed with `no default toolchain configured` - a toolchain failure recorded as an example that does not compile. Fixed in the lane's own verifier: RUSTUP_HOME is named explicitly in the subprocess environment, from the ambient value, then the machine-local registry, then the home beside the proxy's cargo-home.

a cold `cargo check` with a disposable CARGO_HOME resolves the crate's seven requirements and compiles two native build scripts (zstd-sys, bzip2-sys) in 253 seconds, against core.execution's 300-second hard ceiling. Handled rather than fixed: the crate is checked once per composition in one copied workspace and every fence after it reuses that target directory, returning in about half a second. A crate whose cold check exceeds 300 seconds would be BLOCKED_TOOLCHAIN, and the verifier says so rather than reporting its examples false.

observation_not_a_proposal_but_measured.what: review.py::_quoted_verified_fact folds a presentation finding whenever the quote contains, as a whole word, the bare name of any SUPPORTED public_symbol fact of three characters or more. On this crate's 2,084-symbol surface those bare names include Rust's trait methods `from`, `new` and `fmt`, and the product word `cells`.
observation_not_a_proposal_but_measured.measured: Calling presentation_defect on this bundle's own review.json and facts.json: F01 and F02 matched public_symbol:borderlinestyle.from on the word 'from' in 'build it from a source checkout', F04 matched public_symbol:border.new, F06 matched public_symbol:cells on the product name, F07 matched public_symbol:cellarea.fmt on `cargo fmt`. With the rule disabled, F01 and F02 still fold (installation is deterministic) and F04 still folds earlier in the chain (absence_defect), but F06 and F07 - both on LLM-owned sections - would stand and block BC-10.
observation_not_a_proposal_but_measured.why_it_is_recorded_here: The seal is honest against the code as landed and every check was judged as written, but two of the seven folds rest on an ordinary English word colliding with a symbol name rather than on a reviewer scope defect. Lane D does not own review/ and is not proposing a fix inside this item; it is recorded as PROPOSAL P21 so the owner can decide whether the rule needs a narrower test (a qualified name, a code span, or a casing rule) before more candidates seal through it.

proposals: P21 review/independent/review.py::_quoted_verified_fact matches any SUPPORTED public_symbol bare name of three characters or more as a whole word in a finding's quote. On a large Rust surface that includes `from`, `new`, `fmt` and `cells`, so ordinary English prose folds presentation findings that name nothing verified. Measured on Aspose.Cells for Rust: two of seven findings (F06, F07, both on LLM-owned sections) fold on this rule alone. Narrow it - require the qualified value, or a code span, or a name that is not an ordinary word - without losing item 33's ExportToCSV case.

P22 no rule says an extractor must emit facts in the order a bundle stores them, but the sealed-bytes control requires it: FactsDocument.to_dict writes facts sorted by ID while composition/renderer.py::_dependencies lists the bucket in the facts' own order, so any ecosystem whose extractor emits in manifest order seals a README it cannot re-render (lane D hit it on the first Rust bundle, D17). Fix it once in shared code - sort the bucket in the renderer, or keep FactsDocument's facts sorted at construction - so no future plugin can reintroduce it.
